title: How many CPD hours do CPA Australia members need?
description: CPA Australia CPD under By-Law 4.1: 120 hours a triennium, 20 a year, 10 verifiable ethics hours, record retention, annual reviews and statutory CPD.
shortAnswer: CPA Australia members must complete at least 120 hours of continuing professional development (CPD) in each three-year triennium, with at least 20 hours in every year. Within the 120 hours, By-Law 4.1(b) requires at least 10 hours of ethics and professional responsibility, with a minimum of 2 verifiable ethics hours each year. Members keep records for at least 12 months after each triennium ends and may be selected for CPA Australia's annual CPD review.
keyTakeaways: By-Law 4.1(a) of the CPA Australia By-Laws (effective October 1, 2026) sets 120 hours per triennium with at least 20 hours in each year, and applies to suspended members too.
Ethics has been mandated since October 2023. Trienniums ending in 2026 or later carry the full rule: 2 verifiable ethics hours a year and 10 per triennium, counted within the 120.
A member's triennium starts on January 1 of the year of admission if admitted before June 30, otherwise January 1 of the following year (By-Law 4.3).
Records must show the nature, dates, time and topics of each activity and be kept for at least 12 months after each triennium (By-Law 4.2).
Members who hold a tax agent, auditor, liquidator or other statutory registration must also meet that registration's CPD rules (By-Law 4.5).
regulator: CPA Australia Ltd, under its By-Laws; statutory CPD set separately by bodies such as the Tax Practitioners Board (TPB)
appliesTo: CPA, FCPA and Associate members of CPA Australia, including suspended members
Members holding a Public Practice Certificate
Members who are registered tax or BAS agents, company or SMSF auditors, liquidators or credit and financial services licensees
Employers in CPA Australia's Recognised Employer Program

blocks.text: By-Law 4.1 sets two linked minimums: hours and ethics. Under the [CPA Australia By-Laws effective 1 October 2026](https://www.cpaaustralia.com.au/about-cpa-australia/governance/constitution-and-by-laws/our-by-laws), "Members (including suspended Members), must, in each triennium, undertake at least 120 hours of Continuing Professional Development, of which at least 20 hours must be undertaken in each year of the triennium." By-Law 4.1(b) adds that within the 120 hours, members "must undertake at least 10 hours of Ethics and Professional Responsibility, of which at least 2 hours must be undertaken in each year of the triennium."

Life Members, Honorary Members and members on the Retired Membership List are exempt from both minimums, unless a retired member is subject to the requirements referred to in By-Law 3.11(b). Everyone else, including members working outside Australia, falls under the triennium rule. Members with a statutory registration also carry that registration's CPD obligation in parallel, which is covered below.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects the CPA Australia By-Laws effective October 1, 2026 and CPA Australia's CPD guidance as at November 2026.

sections.heading: When does a CPA Australia triennium start and end?

blocks.text: Each member has a rolling three-year triennium tied to their admission date. By-Law 4.3 deems members admitted before June 30 to have started their triennium on January 1 of that year, and members admitted on or after June 30 to have started on January 1 of the following year. Members admitted before December 31, 1998 have trienniums counted from January 1, 1999.

Because trienniums run on calendar years, every member's annual 20 hour minimum and 2 hour ethics minimum resets on January 1. A practical consequence for employers is that a team's members can be in different years of their triennium at the same time, so a single firm-wide deadline does not work. A [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) with one row per member and their triennium start year avoids that problem.

sections.heading: How does the ethics requirement work?

blocks.text: Ethics is part of the 120 hours, not an addition, and it must be verifiable. CPA Australia's [ethics requirements page](https://www.cpaaustralia.com.au/professional-development/continuing-professional-development/ethics-requirements-for-cpd) states that from October 2023 members must complete "a minimum of two (2) verifiable CPD hours per year on ethics-related topics, and 10 hours every three years".

blocks.text: Verifiable means supported by objective evidence of completion. CPA Australia accepts a certificate of completion or confirmation of attendance for ethics CPD and says that "presentation slides, registration emails, or general course materials are not sufficient for verification purposes." This is stricter than many firms' general CPD logs, so ethics sessions need certificates issued at the time.

sections.heading: Which activities count, and what limits apply?

blocks.text: Most structured learning relevant to the member's role counts, but several categories are capped. CPA Australia's [guide to recording CPD](https://www.cpaaustralia.com.au/professional-development/continuing-professional-development/recording-your-cpd) sets these limits and special rules.

blocks.text: CPA Australia notes that changes to its Recognised Employer Program took effect in May 2025 and may affect how CPD is recorded. Members who rely on employer recognition should check which hours the program still covers, because ethics hours must be individually verifiable regardless.

sections.heading: What records must members keep, and how does the CPD review work?

blocks.text: By-Law 4.2 requires each member to record "the precise nature of their Continuing Professional Development, including dates, time expended and topics covered", retain the record for at least 12 months after the end of each triennium, and produce it on request. CPA Australia's online CPD Diary records its own events automatically; other activities must be entered manually.

CPA Australia reviews the records of selected members each year. The review for the 2023 to 2025 triennium commenced on August 15, 2026, with October 30, 2026 the final date for selected members to update their records and outcomes due in November 2026. Records are assessed against key requirements, including relevance to the member's career path.

Under By-Law 4.4, a member who does not complete the required hours or cannot produce a record can be required to enter a formal agreement to make up the shortfall within a set timeframe. Failing to follow that direction is a breach of a membership requirement that can lead to a professional conduct penalty or referral. The evidence approach in [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) applies directly.

sections.heading: How does CPA Australia CPD interact with statutory CPD?

blocks.text: Statutory requirements sit on top of the By-Laws. By-Law 4.5 says members who hold a registration such as company or SMSF auditor, liquidator, tax or BAS agent, trustee in bankruptcy, financial services licensee or credit licensee "must meet any prescribed minimum Continuing Professional Development requirements to maintain such registrations", and By-Law 4.6 requires compliance with applicable APESB standards.

For tax agents the overlap is managed by the [Tax Practitioners Board](https://www.tpb.gov.au/continuing-professional-education), which accepts compliance with a recognized professional association's CPE requirements as meeting its own, provided the activities are relevant to the services provided and meet the TPB's minimum hours. Details are on the page about [TPB continuing professional education requirements](/regulations/tax-practitioners-board-cpe-requirements). Members advising on financial products should also check [financial adviser education and CPD requirements](/regulations/financial-adviser-education-and-cpd-requirements).

The By-Laws also link CPD to public practice. An applicant who previously held a Public Practice Certificate must show 40 hours of CPD referable to public accounting services in the 12 months before re-applying, and those hours count toward the general By-Law 4.1 requirement. Firms in the [professional services sector](/industries/professional-services) often run one CPD plan that satisfies the By-Laws, the TPB and audit regulators at once.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry tags each learning activity with its CPA Australia category, whether it is verifiable, and any statutory registration it also serves, so a firm can see the By-Law position and the TPB position from one record. Ethics activities are linked to completion evidence when delivered, which is the evidence CPA Australia's review asks for.

faqs.q: Can CPA Australia members carry extra hours into the next year?
faqs.a: The By-Laws set a 120 hour triennium total with a 20 hour floor each year, so hours above 20 in one year help reach the triennium total. They do not reduce the 20 hour minimum or the 2 hour ethics minimum in any other year.

faqs.q: Do ethics hours have to come from CPA Australia?
faqs.a: No. Ethics CPD from other providers counts if it relates to ethics and professional responsibility and is supported by verifiable evidence such as a certificate of completion or confirmation of attendance. Slides or registration emails alone are not enough.

faqs.q: How long must CPA Australia CPD records be kept?
faqs.a: By-Law 4.2 requires records to be kept for at least 12 months after the end of each triennium and produced to CPA Australia on request. Members with statutory registrations may face longer periods; the TPB, for example, expects CPE records to be kept for 5 years.

faqs.q: Do retired CPA Australia members need CPD?
faqs.a: Members on the Retired Membership List, along with Life and Honorary Members, are exempt from the By-Law 4.1 hours and ethics minimums, unless the retired member is subject to the requirements referred to in By-Law 3.11(b).

Ethics: from October 2023, 2 verifiable hours per year and 10 per triennium; trienniums ending 2026 carry full obligation
